Batman: The Killing Joke is a 2016 American animated superhero movie produced by Warner Bros. Animation and distributed by Warner Bros. Pictures. It is based on the graphic novel of the same name by Alan Moore and Brian Bolland. The movie is directed by Sam Liu, written by Brian Azzarello and stars the voices of Kevin Conroy, Mark Hamill, Tara Strong, and Ray Wise with Brian George. Like the novel, the movie follows The Joker's kidnapping and mission to drive police commissioner James Gordon insane, and Batman's desperate attempts to stop him. Originally meant to be released directly on home video, due to its popularity, the movie was released in theaters and digitally on July 25, 2016 for a special one-night event, before a DVD and Blu-ray release on August 2, 2016. It grossed $4.4 million worldwide. Critics and fans said that the first half of the film felt unnecessary and disconnected to the second half, although the specific criticism from these viewers is just of ageist, neo-puritanical and bigoted nature, specifically involving the romantic and sexual relationship between Batgirl and Batman already established even in other continuities, so the credibility and reliability of said criticism is dubious to say the least.

Batman: Mask of the Phantasm is a 1993 American animated superhero film based on the DC Comics character Batman. It was directed by Eric Radomski and Bruce Timm and written by Alan Burnett, Paul Dini, Martin Pasko, and Michael Reaves. The film is based on Batman: The Animated Series (1992–1995) and is part of the DC Animated Universe. It was the first film in the DC Animated Universe and the only one in the franchise to receive a wide theatrical release. Kevin Conroy, Mark Hamill, Efrem Zimbalist Jr., Bob Hastings, and Robert Costanzo reprise their voice roles from Batman: The Animated Series. They are joined by Dana Delany, Hart Bochner, Stacy Keach, Abe Vigoda, Dick Miller, and John P. Ryan. The film takes place between the first and second seasons of the television series. It follows Bruce Wayne as he meets his former lover, Andrea Beaumont, while a mysterious vigilante known as the Phantasm begins killing crime bosses in Gotham City. Batman investigates the killings while also trying to discover the Phantasm's identity. The story is partly based on Mike W. Barr's Batman: Year Two comic book story arc. The Reaper, a character from that story, was one of the inspirations for the Phantasm. The film also includes elements from Batman: Year One, particularly its depiction of Bruce Wayne's early attempts to become Batman and fight crime. Mask of the Phantasm was originally planned as a direct-to-video film. Warner Bros. Pictures later decided to release it in theaters, giving the production about eight months to complete the film. It was the first theatrical feature film produced by Warner Bros. Animation. The film was released by Warner Bros. Family Entertainment on December 25, 1993. The film received generally positive reviews from critics. Reviewers praised its animation, voice acting, story, and music. However, its late decision to receive a theatrical release gave the film little time for promotion, and it earned about $5.8 million at the box office, below its $6 million budget. It later became more successful through home media releases. Until the limited theatrical release of Batman: The Killing Joke in 2016, Mask of the Phantasm was the only animated Batman film to receive a theatrical release. It remained the only Batman animated film to receive a wide theatrical release until The Lego Batman Movie was released in 2017. Years before the main events of the film, a young Bruce Wayne returns to Gotham City after years of training abroad. He promises to fight crime in memory of his murdered parents. At first, he tries to stop criminals without using a disguise, but he finds that criminals are not afraid of him. He decides that he needs a more intimidating identity. Bruce meets Andrea Beaumont at Gotham Cemetery while she is visiting her mother's grave. They begin a relationship, and Bruce eventually proposes to her. Bruce is unsure whether to keep his promise to his parents or build a life with Andrea. Andrea and her father, businessman Carl Beaumont, suddenly leave Gotham, however. Andrea sends Bruce a Dear John letter, ending their relationship. Bruce is deeply affected by her departure and eventually becomes Batman. He converts a cave beneath Wayne Manor into the Batcave and begins fighting crime as a masked vigilante. In the present, Batman interrupts mobster Chuckie Sol and his associates while they are planning to launder counterfeit money. Sol escapes but crashes his car while being pursued by the Phantasm, a mysterious masked vigilante whose appearance resembles the Grim Reaper. Sol dies in the crash. Witnesses believe Batman is responsible for his death, and Councilman Arthur Reeves announces that he intends to have Batman arrested. Mobster Buzz Bronski visits Sol's grave at Gotham Cemetery. The Phantasm appears and kills Bronski. Bronski's bodyguards mistake the Phantasm for Batman. While investigating the murder, Batman visits his parents' grave and encounters Andrea. She realizes that Bruce is Batman. Batman discovers that Sol, Bronski, and another mobster, Salvatore Valestra, were connected to Carl Beaumont. Batman questions Andrea, but she says that she does not know where her father is. Valestra, who is elderly and seriously ill, becomes afraid that Batman will kill him next. He asks Reeves for help, but Reeves refuses. Valestra then contacts the Joker and offers him $5 million to kill Batman. The Phantasm also goes to Valestra's penthouse, but finds that the Joker has already killed him. The Joker has attached a camera to Valestra's body so that he can see the Phantasm's identity. He then detonates explosives in the building. The Phantasm escapes, while Batman arrives and is pursued by the police. Andrea helps Batman escape. Andrea later explains to Bruce that her father had worked for Valestra and had taken money from the mob. When Carl could not repay the money, he and Andrea fled to Europe. Carl later became wealthy and offered to repay the mob, but the mob refused to cancel the contract on his life. Andrea returned to Gotham to stop her father from killing his former associates. Bruce and Andrea consider restarting their relationship. Bruce later studies an old photograph of Valestra and the other mobsters and realizes that Valestra's former enforcer was the Joker before his disfigurement. The Joker confronts Reeves and accuses him of helping the mob. A telephone call from Andrea causes the Joker to suspect that she is the Phantasm. The Joker poisons Reeves with his toxin, and Reeves is taken to a hospital. Batman forces Reeves to admit that he was once the Beaumonts' lawyer and helped them hide from the mob. Reeves had asked Carl to support his first election campaign, but Carl refused. Reeves then revealed the Beaumonts' location to Valestra in exchange for the mob's support. Batman visits Andrea's apartment while she is away and finds a message from the Joker. The message suggests that the Joker knows Andrea is the Phantasm. Batman survives an explosion that destroys the apartment. He concludes that the Joker, the last surviving member of Valestra's former group, killed Carl Beaumont as part of the mob's plan. Batman realizes that Andrea has gone after the Joker. Andrea confronts the Joker at the abandoned Gotham World's Fair. The Joker attempts to trap and kill her, but Batman arrives and saves her. Batman asks Andrea to stop seeking revenge, but she refuses. The Joker tries to escape, but Batman stops him. Andrea then takes the Joker with her as the fairgrounds explode. Bruce survives the explosion and returns to the Batcave. Alfred comforts him and tells him that he could not have stopped Andrea from seeking revenge. Bruce then finds Andrea's locket, which contains an old photograph of Bruce and Andrea together. Andrea leaves Gotham aboard an ocean liner. Batman returns to watching over the city. Hart Bochner as City Councilman Arthur Reeves Stacy Keach as Carl Beaumont and the Phantasm Abe Vigoda as Salvatore "The Wheezer" Valestra Bob Hastings as Commissioner James "Jim" Gordon Robert Costanzo as Detective Harvey Bullock Ed Gilbert as Doctor, Police Dispatch, Jake, and Dougan Jeff Bennett as Burton Earny, Helicopter Cop #1, Police Officer, and Laughing Biker Thug Charles Howerton as Helicopter Cop #2 and Thug Judi M. Durand as World of the Future Fair Announcer (uncredited) Dan Castellaneta as Additional Voices (uncredited) Tress MacNeille as Additional Voices (uncredited) Following the success of the first season of Batman: The Animated Series on Fox, Warner Bros. Pictures assigned Alan Burnett to write a story for a feature-length animated film. The original idea involved Batman being captured by his enemies at Arkham Asylum. The villains would then put him on trial in a kangaroo court, blaming him for turning them into criminals. However, the idea was considered "too brainy" because it required Batman to remain inactive for much of the story. It was later adapted into the episode "Trial", which aired after the film's release. Although the Joker has an important role in the film, Burnett wanted to tell a story that focused less on the television series' usual rogues gallery. He also wanted to explore Bruce Wayne's romantic life. Burnett explained, "I wanted to do a love story with Bruce because no one had really done it on the TV show. I wanted a story that got into his head." Some members of the creative team have said that the Joker was not originally intended to appear in the film. However, Paul Dini disagreed with this account. In 2017, he stated that the Joker had been part of the story from the beginning, although his role was secondary to that of the Phantasm. The writers were careful about including the Joker because they wanted to avoid connecting the film too closely to Tim Burton's 1989 film Batman. However, writer Michael Reaves later explained that they realized the Joker could serve the story in a way that would not have been possible in a live-action film. To keep the Joker as the film's main villain apart from the Phantasm, Bruce Timm and Burnett persuaded Dini not to include Harley Quinn. However, Arleen Sorkin voiced a minor character in the film. The creative team had used a similar approach in the episodes "The Strange Secret of Bruce Wayne" and "Joker's Wild". In contrast, the episode "Harley's Holiday" featured Harley Quinn without the Joker. Burnett worked with several other writers to complete the screenplay. Martin Pasko wrote most of the flashback scenes, Reaves wrote the climax, and Dini contributed to various parts of the script. The 1941 film Citizen Kane, directed by Orson Welles, influenced the flashback sequences, which explore loss and the passage of time. According to voice actor Kevin Conroy, the character Andrea Beaumont was named after voice director Andrea Romano. Burnett named Hazel, the robot cook at the World of the Future Fair, after Hazel the Maid. The character was played by Shirley Booth in the television series Hazel, which was based on the comic strip by Ted Key that appeared in The Saturday Evening Post. The design of the Phantasm went through 20 different versions before the filmmakers settled on the final appearance. Burnett described the character as resembling the Grim Reaper wearing a cape. The design was also influenced by the Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come from Charles Dickens' novel A Christmas Carol. The Joker also refers to this resemblance in the finished film. Early in production, Warner Bros. decided to release Batman: Mask of the Phantasm in theaters instead of releasing it directly on video. This decision gave the filmmakers less than a year to complete the film. Most animated feature films take more than two years to produce, from the completion of the story to the final release. The filmmakers also had to change the layout of some scenes to fit the widescreen aspect ratio used for theatrical releases. Warner Bros. gave the filmmakers considerable creative freedom. Warner Bros. also increased the film's budget to $6 million. This allowed the filmmakers to create more detailed and ambitious scenes. The opening title sequence featured a flight through a computer-generated (CGI) version of Gotham City. Sequence director Kevin Altieri also used the city's miniature automated model during the film's climax. In this scene, Batman and the Joker appear as giants compared to the model city. The scene paid tribute to the work of Dick Sprang, a comic book artist known for showing Batman fighting among oversized objects. The New Batman Adventures later paid tribute to Sprang's work in the episode "Legends of the Dark Knight". The film was completed in eight months. Its animation was produced by two overseas studios that regularly worked on Batman: The Animated Series. Dong Yang Animation in South Korea handled most of the animation, while Spectrum Animation in Japan worked on the scene layouts. The film's story has similarities to the 1987 comic book storyline "Batman: Year Two", written by Mike W. Barr and illustrated by Alan Davis and Todd McFarlane. Both stories feature a mysterious villain known as the Reaper in Year Two and the Phantasm in the film. Bruce Timm described Year Two as an "accidental inspiration" for the design of the Phantasm. He said that he had not deliberately based the character's appearance on the Reaper, despite their visual and thematic similarities. Alan Burnett explained that he instead based the Phantasm's methods on Mysterio, a villain from Spider-Man comics. Burnett was particularly interested in the idea of a character who could disappear into smoke. However, Barr believed that the similarities between Mask of the Phantasm and Year Two were intentional. In May 2017, he said that he had visited the Batman: The Animated Series production offices twice and had seen different staff members working with copies of Batman: Year Two beside them. He said these visits first made him aware that the comic storyline might have influenced the film. The early designs of the Phantasm further convinced him that the film had used ideas from his work. Barr then discussed financial compensation with Paul Levitz at DC Comics. Barr said that he wanted to resolve the matter within the company. He was subsequently given a share of the film's earnings and received payment for the creation of the Phantasm. Paul Dini intended each flashback showing Bruce Wayne's romantic life to become more tragic. He wanted the audience to hope that things would improve, only for them to get worse. Bruce's relationship with Andrea Beaumont begins happily but eventually ends in heartbreak. The two plan to marry, but Bruce later receives a note from Andrea ending their relationship. Her decision leads Bruce to return to his plans to become Batman, which he had previously abandoned so that he could build a life with her. Film critic Richard Corliss of Time compared this moment to Andrea's decision to avenge her parents after finding her father murdered. Like Bruce, Andrea gives up the possibility of a happy life and chooses revenge instead. These events change both characters: Bruce becomes Batman, while Andrea becomes the Phantasm. In one scene, Bruce visits his parents' tombstone and says, "I didn't count on being happy." Writer Michael Reaves considered this an important moment in Bruce's life because it shows him giving up the chance to live a normal life. Reaves also explained the significance of Bruce putting on the Batman costume for the first time after Andrea ends their engagement. When Alfred reacts by saying, "My God!", he realizes that Bruce, whom he has helped raise since childhood, has allowed his desire for revenge to take control of his life. Reaves described this moment as Bruce finally accepting the darkness that has consumed him. The film's soundtrack was composed by Shirley Walker, who was also the main composer for Batman: The Animated Series. Walker considered the film's score one of her favorite compositions. In an interview with Cinemusic.com, Walker explained that the Latin-sounding lyrics in the main title sequence were actually the names of key Warner Bros. staff members played backward. The song "I Never Even Told You" was written by Siedah Garrett and Glen Ballard and performed by Tia Carrere. Hans Zimmer also played the synthesizer on the score. He later composed the music for Christopher Nolan's The Dark Knight Trilogy and the film Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice. Reprise Records first released the soundtrack on December 14, 1993. On March 24, 2009, La-La Land Records released a limited-edition expanded version of the soundtrack. This edition includes all the tracks from the original release, with some tracks presented in longer versions. It also contains almost 30 minutes of music that had not been released before. In December 1993, two novelizations of the film were published. One was a book for young readers written by Andrew Helfer, with contributions from Alan Burnett. The other was a novel for adult readers written by Geary Gravel. DC Comics published a comic book adaptation written by Kelley Puckett and illustrated by Mike Parobeck. The comic adaptation was later included with the film's VHS release. Kenner, which had already produced toys based on Batman: The Animated Series, released several action figures based on the film. These included figures of the Joker and the Phantasm. The Phantasm figure was packaged without its mask, revealing the character's identity before viewers watched the film. In 1996, DC Comics published Batman & Robin Adventures Annual #1: Shadow of the Phantasm, a comic book sequel written by Paul Dini. In 2015, DC Collectibles released a two-figure set featuring Batman and the Phantasm. Mask of the Phantasm was released on LaserDisc in April 1994 and on VHS in May 1994. In April 2003, the VHS release was reissued as part of a three-tape set with Batman & Mr. Freeze: SubZero and Batman Beyond: Return of the Joker. The film was first released on DVD in December 1999 in a snap case. In April 2004, it was released in a three-disc DVD set with SubZero and Return of the Joker. The film was released again on DVD in October 2005 in a keep case with an insert. In February 2008, Warner Home Video released it as a double feature with SubZero. On July 25, 2017, the film was released on Blu-ray as part of the Warner Archive Collection. This release included new high-definition transfers in both 16:9 widescreen and open matte 4:3 formats. In late 2018, the film was also included in the Blu-ray box set of Batman: The Complete Animated Series. Batman: Mask of the Phantasm was released in theaters in the United States on December 25, 1993. It earned $1.2 million during its first two days in 1,506 theaters. The film earned a total of $5.8 million at the domestic box office. The filmmakers blamed Warner Bros. Pictures for the film's unsuccessful marketing campaign. They believed the studio's late decision to release the film in theaters had left too little time to promote it. Despite its poor box office performance, the film eventually made a profit through home media sales. The film received generally positive reviews from critics. According to Rotten Tomatoes, 83% of critics gave the film a positive review, with an average rating of 7.1 out of 10 based on 58 reviews. Metacritic gave the film a score of 65 out of 100 based on 18 reviews, indicating "generally favorable" reviews. Empire named it one of the best animated films of 1993 and praised its story, which the magazine considered stronger than those of Tim Burton's Batman and Batman Returns. TV Guide Magazine praised the film's Art Deco style and film noir influences. It also highlighted the action scenes, including the climax and Batman's escape from the Gotham City Police Department. Richard Harrington of The Washington Post praised the film's animation, design, dialogue, story, and musical score by Shirley Walker. Gene Siskel and Roger Ebert also gave the film a positive review on their television program At the Movies when it was released on home video. Siskel considered it better than Batman Returns and Joel Schumacher's Batman Forever, and slightly less good than the 1989 film Batman. Not all reviews were positive. Chris Hicks of the Deseret News felt that the film only became engaging during its third act. He also believed that the filmmakers had sacrificed some of the visual elements to focus on the story. Leonard Klady of Variety gave the film a mostly negative review. He criticized its themes as clichéd and described parts of the animation as resembling self-parody. Over time, the film appeared on several lists of the greatest animated and superhero films. In 2010, IGN ranked it among its 25 best animated films of all time. The website also described it as Batman's best big-screen story up to that point, before the release of Batman Begins. In 2011, Total Film ranked the film 47th on its list of the 50 greatest animated films. Time included it on its list of the ten best superhero films in 2011. In 2017, Screen Rant named it the best Batman film of all time. In 2018, Paste magazine called it the greatest Batman film. In 2022, Empire also named it the best Batman film. That same year, Rolling Stone ranked it 19th on its list of the 50 greatest superhero films of all time. It was the only traditionally animated film on the list, the third-highest-ranked animated superhero film, and the second-highest-ranked Batman film, behind The Dark Knight. In 2022, actor Robert Pattinson, who played Batman in Matt Reeves' film The Batman, cited Mask of the Phantasm as an example of a film that explored Batman's inner thoughts and psychology. To mark the film's 20th anniversary, a screening was held in Santa Monica, California, with voice actors Kevin Conroy, Dana Delany, and Mark Hamill attending. To mark its 25th anniversary, Fathom Events rereleased the film in theaters for one day on November 12, 2018. Mask of the Phantasm was nominated for the Annie Award for Best Animated Feature alongside The Lion King and The Nightmare Before Christmas. It lost to The Lion King.

Batman: Caped Crusader is an American animated television series based on the DC Comics character Batman. The series is created by Bruce Timm, and produced by Bad Robot Productions, 6th & Idaho Motion Picture Company, DC Entertainment, Warner Bros. Animation, and Amazon MGM Studios. It premiered on August 1, 2024, on Amazon Prime Video to very positive reviews from critics and audience members. The show is noir-inspired, focusing on a young Bruce Wayne during the early years as Batman in Gotham City.

Batman (Terry McGinnis) is a character from the animated television series Batman Beyond. He is a futuristic version of the DC Comics superhero Batman who takes on the mantle in a cyberpunk Gotham City. Terry McGinnis is a high school student who becomes Batman under the mentorship of an aging Bruce Wayne. He wears a high-tech Batsuit with advanced gadgets, enhanced strength, and flight capabilities. His story explores themes of legacy, responsibility, and adapting to a dystopian future.

Batman: Mask of the Phantasm (Original Motion Picture Soundtrack) is the soundtrack album for the 1993 animated superhero film. The music was composed by Shirley Walker, who also composed music for Batman: The Animated Series (1992–1995). Reprise Records released the soundtrack on December 14, 1993. The album contains 11 tracks, including the song "I Never Even Told You", which was written by Siedah Garrett and Glen Ballard and performed by Tia Carrere. On March 24, 2009, La-La Land Records released a limited edition of the soundtrack. The release was limited to 3,000 copies and included the complete film score, along with previously unreleased music by Walker. The music composed by Danny Elfman for the 1989 film Batman influenced Walker's music for both Batman: The Animated Series and Batman: Mask of the Phantasm. In an interview with Cinemusic.com, Walker explained that the Latin-sounding words heard in the film's main title theme were actually the names of members of the music team spoken backwards. The music team had to finish its work before the film's final dubbing process was complete. Walker also worked to ensure that the supporting music team members received credit for their work. She created the lyrics by arranging syllables from each musician's name in reverse order. She also received help from several members of Warner Bros. staff. Walker spent more time writing the lyrics than recording the choir music. By the time the choir recorded the music, two Warner Bros. staff members had already worked out the meaning of the words. Walker thought that the singers might find the unusual lyrics difficult to sing, but she said that they enjoyed recording them. During the mixing process, Bobby Fernandez recorded the choir singing without instruments, known as a cappella, onto a separate tape for Walker's sample reel. By the end of the recording process, each person had a tape of the choir singing their name. Hans Zimmer, who later composed the music for The Dark Knight Trilogy, played the synthesizer for the film's score. He also played the synthesizer for Batman: The Animated Series. The score received critical acclaim and has been described as one of Shirley Walker's best compositions. It was also reported to be one of her favorite scores. Angelo Delos Trinos of Comic Book Resources praised the score for its Gothic atmosphere and haunting sound. He wrote that Walker's music emphasized the tragic elements of Batman: Mask of the Phantasm and compared the film's score to an opera. He also considered it stronger than the score for The Batman (2022). Kenneth Lowe of Paste praised the score's choral elements and its role in establishing the film's tone. He noted that, although the story has relatively small stakes for Gotham City, it explores the personal struggles of Batman and Bruce Wayne in greater depth. Rodolfo Salas of Screen Rant highlighted the score's use of operatic vocals and themes from Batman: The Animated Series. He noted that Walker's experience working on the series helped her preserve its musical style while expanding it for the film. Evan Krell of Mxdwn noted that the score pays tribute to Danny Elfman's earlier Batman music while developing its own distinct sound. Jason Wiese of CinemaBlend praised the score's use during action scenes and flashbacks to Bruce Wayne's relationship with Andrea Beaumont, voiced by Dana Delany. He also noted how the music reflects Bruce's struggle between love and revenge, describing it as an important part of the film's success. In 2016, Sean Wilson of Den of Geek included the score in his list of the 25 greatest superhero film scores. He praised its emotional depth and compared it favorably to Elfman's music for Batman (1989). In 2018, Charlie Brigden of Film School Rejects included it on a list of great film scores by female composers. He highlighted the use of a theremin in the Phantasm theme and the choral music accompanying Bruce Wayne's transformation into Batman. Batman Forever is a 1995 American superhero movie directed by Joel Schumacher and based on the DC Comics character Batman. It stars Val Kilmer as Batman. Tommy Lee Jones, Jim Carrey, Nicole Kidman, Chris O'Donnell, Michael Gough, and Pat Hingle also act. This movie was released on June 16, 1995 across the United States. It has a $100 million, and grossed over $336.6 million at the box office. It got mixed reviews from the critics. Originally intended as a sequel to Batman Returns with Michael Keaton and Michelle Pfeiffer reprising their roles and Tim Burton supposed to come back to direct, the movie was instead turned into a reboot and is the first installment of Joel Schumacher's Batman duology. Despite this Michael Gough, and Pat Hingle played Alfred and Commissioner Gordon again.

Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice is an American superhero movie. It is based on the DC Comics characters Superman, Batman and Wonder Woman. It was co-produced by Dune Entertainment and Syncopy Films. It was distributed by Warner Bros. The movie is the sequel to 2013's Man of Steel and the second installment in the DC Extended Universe. The movie was directed by Zack Snyder. It was written by Chris Terrio, from a screenplay by David S. Goyer. Gotham City's own vigilante, Batman, travels to Metropolis to take on Superman, fearing what would happen if the latter is kept unchecked. As Batman and Superman confront one another, they realise they were wrong about each other, Superman isn't some genocidal warlord and Batman isn't some lowlife vigilante. They became best buddy after Superman sacrificed himself to save the world and later came back to life. Also, Lois was pregnant with Clarke's child at the time. Henry Cavill as Clark Kent / Superman: A Kryptonian survivor and a journalist for the Daily Planet who uses his superhuman abilities to protect the Earth. Ben Affleck as Bruce Wayne / Batman: A billionaire socialite and owner of Wayne Enterprises who dedicates himself to protect Gotham City from its criminal underworld as a highly trained, masked vigilante. Amy Adams as Lois Lane: a reporter for the Daily Planet and love interest of Clark Kent. Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor: A sophisticated young businessman and hereditary CEO of LexCorp who is fixated on defeating who he considers as his archenemy, Superman. He is the primary antagonist of the film. Diane Lane as Martha Kent: Clark's adoptive mother. Laurence Fishburne as Perry White: the editor-in-chief of the Daily Planet and Clark and Lois' boss. Jeremy Irons as Alfred Pennyworth: Bruce Wayne's butler, chief of security and trusted confidant. Holly Hunter as Senator June Finch: a United States Senator. Gal Gadot as Diana Prince / Wonder Woman: a 5,000-year-old Amazonian princess, and daughter of Zeus. Additionally, Tao Okamoto plays Mercy Graves, Luthor's assistant. Scoot McNairy plays Wallace Keefe, an employee of Wayne Enterprises who is injured during the final events of Man of Steel and becomes a pawn in Lex's planl Patrick Wilson plays the President of the United States. Callan Mulvey plays Anatoli Knyazev. Michael Cassidy plays Jimmy Olsen. Jeffrey Dean Morgan and Lauren Cohan play Thomas and Martha Wayne, Bruce Wayne's deceased parents. Robin Atkin Downes voices Doomsday. Repeating their roles from Man of Steel are Harry Lennix as Secretary Calvin Swanwick, Christina Wren as Major Carrie Farris, Michael Shannon as General Zod, and Carla Gugino as the Kryptonian A.I. Kelor. Ray Fisher, Jason Momoa and Ezra Miller appear as Victor Stone / Cyborg, Arthur Curry / Aquaman and Barry Allen / The Flash respectively in cameo appearances, which will lead into their inclusion in the Justice League film. Senator Patrick Leahy makes a cameo appearances as himself. Jena Malone was cast as Barbara Gordon, but her scenes were cut from the theatrical release. They will appear in the Ultimate Edition home media release. The success of Man of Steel made Warner Bros. plans of a cinematic universe featuring other DC Comics characters. In June 2013, it was announced that director Zack Snyder and screenwriter David S. Goyer would both be returning for a Man of Steel sequel, which is being fast tracked by Warner Bros. Goyer had previously signed a three-movie deal, which includes Man of Steel, its sequel, and a Justice League movie featuring Superman. The following month, Snyder confirmed at San Diego Comic-Con International that the sequel to Man of Steel would have Superman and Batman meeting for the first time in a movie. Cavill, Adams, Lane, and Fishburne will repeat their roles. Snyder said that the movie would take inspiration from the comic The Dark Knight Returns. In August 2013, Ben Affleck was announced to be playing Batman. Gal Gadot was cast as Wonder Woman in December 2013. Later in December, Argo screenwriter Chris Terrio was hired to rewrite the script, due to Goyer's commitments in other projects. In January 2014, it was announced that the movie had been delayed from its original July 17, 2015 release date to May 6, 2016, and in May 2014, the movie's title was revealed to be Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice. The date was moved again to March 25, 2016. Pre-production began at East Los Angeles College in October 2013, with principal photography starting in May 2014 in Detroit, Michigan and in Chicago, Illinois. With a production budget of $410 million, Batman v Superman is the most expensive film ever made at the time of its release, even after adjusting for inflation. Filming began in 2013. Shooting locations were in Detroit, Michigan, Los Angeles, California, and Chicago, Illinois.

Batman Begins is a 2005 stealth/action-adventure video game based on the 2005 movie Batman Begins. It has all of the cast returning except Gary Oldman. It was also going to be released for the PlayStation Portable but got cancelled. The game starts out with Batman at the Narrows before going through a tutorial set during the movie's start. Batman vs. Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles is a 2019 animated crossover superhero movie, directed by Jake Castorena, written by Marly Halpern-Graser, and produced by Warner Bros. Animation, DC Entertainment, and Nickelodeon. The movie is an adaptation of the six-issue inter-company crossover comic book miniseries Batman/Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles by James Tynion IV and Freddie Williams II. The story focuses on Batman, Robin and Batgirl teaming up with the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, in order to save Gotham City from chaos at the hands of both Shredder and Ra's al Ghul with their sect: the Foot Clan and the League of Assassins. The movie itself features the voices of Troy Baker, Darren Criss, Eric Bauza, Cas Anvar and Andrew Kishino. The movie is the first collaboration between Warner Bros. and Nickelodeon, and was devised for the direct-to-video market. It was released on both Blu-ray and Digital HD on June 4, 2019. It was well-liked, and grossed over $3.8 million from sales. Jim Meskimen as Commissioner Gordon and Dr. Jonathan Crane / Scarecrow Keith Ferguson as Dr. Baxter Stockman and Harvey Dent / Two-Face Tara Strong as Dr. Harleen Quinzel / Harley Quinn, Dr. Pamela Isley / Poison Ivy and Pizza Delivery Girl John DiMaggio as Dr. Victor Fries / Mr. Freeze Warner Bros. Animation was considering adaptations of Batman/Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles and Wonder Woman as possible direct-to-video movies. The animated adaptation of the miniseries was officially announced in February 2019 to be in production and was released later in the spring. The initial announcement revealed Troy Baker would reprise his roles as both Batman from Batman: The Telltale Series video game and various Lego video games and movies, and the Joker from Batman: Arkham Origins, Batman: Assault on Arkham, and the Batman Unlimited series, making Baker the first actor to portray both characters in the same property. The movie also features Darren Criss and Eric Bauza reprising their roles as Raphael and Leonardo, while Kyle Mooney and Baron Vaughn voice Michelangelo and Donatello, respectively. Rachel Bloom voices Batgirl and Cas Anvar voices Ra's al Ghul. In addition, Tom Kenny, John DiMaggio, Carlos Alazraqui and Tara Strong reprise their roles as the Penguin, Mr. Freeze, Bane, Harley Quinn and Poison Ivy from various DC properties. Other key cast members of the movie were revealed a month later, which consists of Ben Giroux as Robin, Andrew Kishino as the Shredder, Keith Ferguson as both Baxter Stockman and Two-Face, Brian George reprising his role as Alfred Pennyworth from Batman: The Killing Joke, and Jim Meskimen as both Commissioner James Gordon and the Scarecrow. The first trailer was released on March 12, 2019. The movie had its world premiere at WonderCon Anaheim 2019 on March 31. The movie was later released to Digital on May 14 on 4K Ultra HD Combo Pack and Blu-ray Combo Pack on June 4, 2019. Batman vs. Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles was well-liked. Based on 13 reviews collected on Rotten Tomatoes, the movie has an approval rating of 100% with an average rating of a 7.47/10. The movie earned $3,898,811 from domestic home video sales.

Batman Beyond is a popular animated television series that aired from January 10, 1999 to December 18, 2001 and is set in the DC Animated Universe. Based on the DC Comics superhero Batman, it features Terry McGinnis as the new Batman, operating in a futuristic Gotham City under the guidance of an elderly Bruce Wayne. The show explores themes of legacy, technology, and heroism in a cyberpunk-inspired world.

A Marine Staff Sergeant played by Aaron Eckhart leads a platoon of U.S. Marines and other stranded military personnel, during a global alien invasion. Battle Beyond the Stars is a 1980 American science fiction western movie directed by Jimmy T. Murakami and screenplay by John Sayles. It stars George Peppard, Robert Vaughn, Richard Thomas, John Saxon, Sybil Danning and it was distributed by New World Pictures.

Battle for the Planet of the Apes is a 1973 American science fiction movie directed by J. Lee Thompson and is the fifth and final movie in the original Planet of the Apes series. It stars Roddy McDowall, Claude Akins, Natalie Trundy, Severn Darden, Lew Ayres, John Huston, Austin Stoker, France Nuyen and John Landis and was distributed by 20th Century Fox. Battle for the Planet of the Apes was the final Planet of the Apes movie to be rated G.

Battle Fever J is a Japanese television series. It is the 3rd in Toei's Super Sentai series. Battle Fever J was a co-production of Toei Company and Marvel Comics. A total of 52 episodes aired on TV Asahi between February 3, 1979 and January 26, 1980. The team have codenames named for countries around the world, also respectively named in their theme song: Battle France, Battle Cossack (Soviet Union), Battle Kenya, Miss America (United States) and Battle Japan. This was the first series in the Super Sentai franchise where the heroes must control giant robots to defeat a monster who itself has grown to a gigantic size. Battle Fever J also marks the first appearance of a Black and Orange Ranger in the franchise. Toei's tokusatsu adaptation of Spider-Man was the first to introduce this format and was also the inspiration for this series. The series was also partially inspired by the Marvel Comics character Captain America. Battle Fever J was also the first series to use the term Super Sentai (unlike the previous two who were just called Sentai, without the "Super") until Toei announced in 1995 that its predecessors Himitsu Sentai Gorenger and J.A.K.Q. Dengekitai were also part of the Super Sentai series, when Chouriki Sentai Ohranger was announced as the 19th Super Sentai team. General Kurama assembles four young agents who had been dispatched around the world for training. They are joined by FBI investigator Diane Martin, whose father was murdered by Egos. The five don powered suits to become the Battle Fever team. The Battle Fever team's trump card is the Battle Fever Robo. Egos tries to stop the construction of the Robot. Although the monsters they send to perform this task are defeated one by one by the Fever team. Egos then unleashes the "younger brother" of the Buffalo Monster, a giant robot replica of its "older brother". The Robot, fortunately, is finished in time. Aboard it, the Fever team defeats the Buffalo Monster and its successors. The Fever team never stops, even when is lost two of its members (the original Miss America and Battle Cossack). With new members, the team defeats Hedder, now the Hedder Monster, and breaks into Egos' headquarters, where they are fed into the Egos Monster Making Machine so that they may be used as material for a Battle Fever Monster. The team destroys the machine and slays the mysterious deity Satan Egos himself with the Lightning Sword Rocketter sword-throwing move. Battle for Dream Island (BFDI) is an animated web series created by Cary and Michael Huang in 2010. The series is a parody of game shows, starring characters that are anthropomorphic objects, meaning that they are nonliving objects which have been given human traits. Around 2012, inspired a subgenre of similar web series called "object shows". The term object show refers to an animated series that includes anthropomorphic object characters (objects with human traits), usually with simple designs, who compete in Survivor-style competitions. The fandom is often referred to as the "object show community", or "OSC" for short. One example of this is Inanimate Insanity, created by Adam Katz in 2011. Two writers of II—Joseph Pak and Samuel Thornbury—worked on BFDI as showrunners.

Battle of Britain is a 1969 British Second World War movie directed by Guy Hamilton, and produced by Harry Saltzman and S. Benjamin Fisz. The movie is about the Battle of Britain. It stars Laurence Olivier as Air Chief Marshal Sir Hugh Dowding, Trevor Howard as Air Vice-Marshal Keith Park, and Patrick Wymark as Air Vice-Marshal Trafford Leigh-Mallory, Air Officer commanding No. 12 Group RAF. It also starred Michael Caine, Christopher Plummer and Robert Shaw as Squadron Leaders.

Battle of Warsaw 1920 is a 2011 Polish historical movie directed by Jerzy Hoffman and starring Daniel Olbrychski, Borys Szyc, Andrzej Strzelecki, Ewa Wiśniewska, Olga Kabo, Adam Ferency, Jacek Poniedziałek, Wiktor Zborowski, Wojciech Pszoniak.

Nihonkai daikaisen ( Battle of the Japan Sea) is a 1969 Japanese war drama film directed by Seiji Maruyama and produced by Tomoyuki Tanaka. Set between 1904 and 1905, Japan and Russia clash in what comes to be known as the Russo-Japanese War. An attempt by the Japanese fleet and army to take Port Arthur fails, and a Russian fleet bears down on the Sea of Japan. Veteran screenwriter Toshio Yasumi wrote the script and Seiji Maruyama (who had filmed Rengo kantai shirei chôkan: Yamamoto Isoroku in 1968) directed the film. Special effects director Eiji Tsuburaya of "Destroy All Monsters" worked on the set and Hiroshi Murai of "Nikudan" was in charge of filming the scenes. The concurrent screening work is "Konto 55-Gō jinrui no dai jakuten", directed by Jun Fukuda. It is said to be the third work in the "Toho 8/15 series", but unlike the two previous war films, this one take place during the Russo-Japanese War. From the beginning of the war, to General Nogi Maresuke's troops attack Port Arthur, and the combined fleet led by Admiral Togo Heihachiro at the Battle of Tsushima to defeats the Baltic Fleet led by Vice Admiral Zinovy Rozhestvensky. This work was the last film in which Eiji Tsuburaya participated it as special effects director. The ship miniature mobilized 60 art designers and 107 ships were prepared for the movie. In addition, the miniature of the battleship Mikasa was made up to 13 meters. In the naval battle scene, considering that the power of the bullets is weaker at the time of the Russo-Japanese War than during the Pacific War, the water column is expressed by freon gas. During the late 19th century, the Qing dynasty continued to disintegrate in turmoil due to corruption, peasant unrest, ruler incompetence, and population growth which led to food shortages and regular famine. In 1900 during the Boxer Rebellion, the Eight Nation Alliance (Britain, United States, Germany, France, Russia, Japan, Italy and Austria-Hungary) joined forces together to occupied many ports and cities in China. However, only Russia kept its troops in Manchuria and set up their railway line which caused tensions with Japan over the sphere of influence. At the Imperial Conferences meeting with Emperor Meiji, they sent an ultimatum to recognize Russian dominance in Manchuria in exchange for recognition of Korea being within the Japanese sphere of influence. Finally, diplomatic relations between two countries began to get worse. Togo Heihachiro, Admiral of the Fleet in the Imperial Japanese Navy, was eyeing Lushunkou (Port Arthur) and the movement of the Russian Pacific Fleet in Vladivostok, and devised a secret plan. He got reports that Captain Takeo Hirose, commanding the old cargo vessel Fukui Maru and several ships, was spotted by the Russian fleet squadron and was hit, destroying the ship and killing Hirose. Many officers and sailors managed to escape from the Battle of Port Arthur. War was declared after the first naval battle. The Japanese Navy won its first battle against the Russians. In the meantime, Japanese troops deployed from Korea to Manchuria. The First Army under General Kuroki Tamemoto landed on Incheon to occupied Seoul and began marching north to meet the Russian army at the Yalu River. After defeating them, the Third Army led by General Nogi Maresuke march on to Port Arthur and began the siege. The Russian Navy was unable to relieve the siege after they were defeated again by the Japanese squadron at Chemulpo Bay. On October 20, the Baltic Fleet left the port of Rabaul. Togo decided that the enemy ships would appear in the Sea of Japan and dragged the combined fleet inland. On New Year's Day, five months after the attack began, General Nogi planned an attack on 203 Hill, trying to capture the fortress. However, the commander of Port Arthur Anatoly Stessel managed to hold off the attack by setting up machine guns, artillery positions, land mines, and searchlights. The Japanese continued to attack the fortress until the defense commander Roman Kondratenko was killed by artillery shells and Stessel had no choice but to surrender the fortress to General Nogi. Around this time, Akashi Motojiro, an intelligence officer in Stockholm (Sweden), learned that the route of the Baltic Fleet would be determined by Russian Vice Admiral Zinovy Rozhestvensky. They discovered the Baltic Fleet headed off to the Goto Islands. Seven days later, Admiral Togo, who hoisted the Z flag on board the flagship Mikasa, took an intrepid tactic that took a big turn in front of the Russians. A fierce battle at Tsushima brought a great victory to the Japanese fleet. People of Japan who are excited about victory and the Russians are forced to surrender in the Treaty of Portsmouth on September 5, 1905. This resulted in Russia a bloody revolution by mass demonstrations over the defeat. However, Togo could not forget the true "fear of battle" by winning the war. Battle of the Bands is an upcoming American independent adult animated series. The show was created by Allissoon Lockhart, who previously worked as a line producer for shows like Inside Job and Gameoverse. Parker Simmons, the creator of Mao Mao: Heroes of Pure Heart, is the co-showrunner. The series is produced by Arin Hanson (Egoraptor), Brent Lilley, and the comedy duo Game Grumps. It is being represented by the Creative Artists Agency (CAA) while the creators pitch it to networks and look for a full release. The show takes place in a world where musicians get elemental powers based on the genre of music they play. The story follows Heatseeker, a five-piece heavy metal band that has just joined a massive tournament. The main characters are twin sisters named Jayme and Brooke Scott. Brooke is the loud, wild lead guitarist, and Jayme is the quiet roadie who wants to write her own music. When problems happen at the start of their tour, the sisters must work together to keep the band from breaking up, win the tournament, and control their magical fire powers. The series creator has shared that the sisters' last name was inspired by Bon Scott, the famous lead singer of the rock band AC/DC. Jayme Scott (voiced by Erica Mendez): The quiet roadie who wants to be a composer. Brooke Scott (voiced by Sarah Natochenny): Jayme's loud twin sister and the lead guitarist of Heatseeker. Kasumi (voiced by Erika Ishii): A member of the band. Toomey (voiced by Imari Williams): The rhythm guitarist of Heatseeker. Jules Joliet (voiced by Arin Hanson): The lead singer of Heatseeker. Rhett (voiced by Matthew Di Panni): A member of the band. The show was first announced with a rough animation clip at San Diego Comic-Con (SDCC) in July 2021. In May 2024, the creators released behind-the-scenes artwork and revealed the main voice cast. In June 2024, they released Heatseeker's first full-length song, called "RISE". The show is currently being made independently. The creator stated that progress takes time because the team is focused on safe and healthy production practices.

Battlestar Galactica is a science fiction franchise. It includes two separate television series, one sequel series, movies, books, comic books, toy and other merchandise. The series are named after the main spacecraft, the Battlestar (a large type of warship in space) Galactica. The first series was created in 1978 after the successful theater release of Star Wars. The series was shown on the American network ABC. The series lasted for eight months and 17 episodes before it ended. The cost of making the series was said to be one of the reasons for it ending. The series starred Lorne Greene as Commander Adama, captain of the Galactica. Richard Hatch played his son, the pilot Apollo. Dirk Benedict played Apollo's friend and fellow pilot, Starbuck. In 1980, ABC made the sequel series Galactica 1980. This series took place after the fleet got to Earth. The series did not do well in the ratings and quickly ended. Several movies were made using edited version of both series. In 2003, Universal Television along with the Sci-Fi Channel and Sky One created a three-hour mini-series based on the original television series. This series was very well liked by both the audience and critics. This led to the Sci-Fi Channel making it into a series in 2004. After the 2007 season of Battlestar Galactica, the Nielsen ratings said that over 119 million people watched the series. This made it the highest rated and most watched series on cable networks. Edward James Olmos plays Commander William Adama. Jamie Bamber plays his son, Lee "Apollo" Adama. Katee Sackhoff plays Kara "Starbuck" Thrace. Starbuck was one of several characters to be changed from a male character into a female character. All of the Battlestar Galactica series have the same basic setting. In a far away part of the universe, a civilization of humans live on planets known as the "Twelve Colonies". In the past, the Colonies were at war with a cybernetic race known as the Cylons. With the help of a human named Gaius Baltar, the Cylons attacked on the Colonies. This surprise attack caused much damage to the planets where the humans lived and killed most of their populations. A few thousand of humans did not die in the attacks. They fled into space aboard any spacecraft they could. Of all the Colonial Fleet, the battlestar Galactica appears to be the only military ship that was not destroyed in the attack. Under the leadership of military leader Commander Adama, the Battlestar Galactica and its crew lead and protect the fleet of survivors into space in search of a fabled Thirteenth Colony and its home planet, Earth.

Battlefield Earth is a 2000 American science fiction movie directed by Roger Christian and starring John Travolta, Barry Pepper, Forest Whitaker and Kelly Preston. It was adapted from the novel of the Scientology founder L. Ron Hubbard. The movie got very poor reviews from movie critics. It also did poorly at the box office, because the money earned from the cinemas was less than half of its budget. It won seven Golden Raspberry Awards. In 2008, it was placed on a list of the ten worse movies of the past ten years. On Rotten Tomatoes, the movie has a positive rating of only 3% from the audience. The movie takes place in the year 3000, when Earth is a ruined wasteland ruled by the Psychlos, who are a brutal race of giant humanoid aliens who have ruled the planet for 1,000 years, and use human slave labor to strip its minerals and other resources, with a special desire for gold. The humans rebel against the aliens.

Battleground is a 1949 American World War II action movie directed by William A. Wellman and stars Van Johnson, John Hodiak, Ricardo Montalbán, George Murphy, Marshall Thompson, James Whitmore, Douglas Fowley. It was distributed by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer and was nominated for 6 Oscars and won 2 Academy Awards in 1950.

Battleship Potemkin (, Bronenosets Potyomkin), sometimes spelled as Battleship Potyomkin is a 1925 silent drama Russian movie directed by Sergei Eisenstein. The movie is about a ship crew rebelling against their officers on the Battleship Potemkin and the events that follow. The film is often considered one of the best movies ever made. The film is set in 1905 and is divided into five acts. The Potemkin is part of the Imperial Russian Navy's Black Sea Fleet. This opening act shows the poor conditions of the crew. Matyushenko and Vakulinchuk are two sailors who talk about the revolution. They want the sailors of the ship to join the revolution. Sailors are sleeping in their hammocks, and an officer beats a sailor. On deck, there appears to be rotten meat. The sailors complain about it and their low rations and refuse to eat it. The men who did not eat meat are ordered to be killed by a firing squad. The sailors with rifles lower their weapons and do not shoot. This is when the uprising starts. Sailors throw officers overboard and take over the ship. However, the leader Vakulinchuk is killed. The Potemkin goes to the shores of Odessa. Sailors display Vakulinchuk's body in public. The people are sad but inspired. They start getting upset about the Tsar and his government. The sailors say goodbye and praise Vakulinchuk as a hero. Many people have come to see the sailors and say goodbye. Suddenly soldiers (Cossack) start shooting at the people on the steps. They continue to march down the steps and shoot at men, women, and children. A baby carriage rolls down the steps, and a woman shot in the face with broken glasses is shown. The people cry out to the soldiers. In response, sailors of Potemkin shoot at the Opera House. There was a meeting there with Tsarist military leaders. The sailors go out into the sea to face the fleet of the Tsar. The sailors of the other ships do not open fire. Instead, they cheer the Potemkin on. Aleksandr Antonov as Grigory Vakulinchuk (Bolshevik sailor) Grigori Aleksandrov as Chief Officer Giliarovsky I. Bobrov as Young sailor flogged while sleeping Beatrice Vitoldi as Woman with the baby carriage Eisenstein wanted the movie to be a propaganda film. Eisenstein wanted viewers to feel sorry for the sailors and support their rebellion. The film was created very emotionally. This was so viewers could sympathize with the characters. Eisenstein uses a lot of montage editing to create emotional effects. Eisenstein was unhappy that not many people watched the movie in Russia. The Odessa Steps sequence is a very famous scene in cinema. It is a classic example of montage theory. It has influenced other movies. Many other movies reference to or parody the scene. George Lucas's Star Wars: Episode III – Revenge of the Sith, Chandrashekhar Narvekar's Hindi film Tezaab, Ettore Scola's We All Loved Each Other So Much. Woody Allen's Bananas and Love and Death; Zucker, Abrahams, and Zucker's Naked Gun 33⅓: The Final Insult (though also a parody of The Untouchables); The short film Mr. Bill Goes to Washington; The German-Turkish film Kebab Connection; and the Italian Fantozzi comedy film Il secondo tragico Fantozzi. There were not too many showings of the film in Russia. In other countries, the movie was controversial at the time. Countries like England, France, Germany and United States banned the movie for some time. Countries were worried that soldiers and sailors would apply the film and rebel against officers. Countries also thought the movie was too violent. Modern critics praise the film as one of the best. The film has a 100% rating on Rotten Tomatoes. The film has a 97% rating on Metacritic. Critics say it is the best in Russian Cinema and that its montage editing is influential. Brussel's World Fair named the film the greatest film of all time in 1958. In 1952, the Sight & Sound magazine ranked the film fourth best out of all films. It got 11th place in the same 2012 poll. The film was also ranked the 11th best film at the British Film Institute poll.
Battlestar Galactica is an American science fiction television series created by Glen A. Larson. It was originally broadcast from September 17, 1978 to April 29, 1979 on ABC.

Battlefield is an Indian Meitei language feature-length, documentary film. It tells stories of the history and myths of World War II happened in Manipur. It shows the incidents of 1944 Battle of Imphal between the Allied Forces and Japan. It is directed by Borun Thokchom. It was produced by Manjoy Lourembam and co-produced by Radheshyam Oinam, of Network Services Imphal, and Vishwamitra Universals. It is 80 minutes in duration. According to director Borun Thokchom, the filming took more than ten years. In "The Hindu" report, it is said to be thirteen years. Rajeshwor Singh was the main character (protagonist) of the film. He was shown doing deep research and fieldwork, making the backbone of the documentary. He took the role of helping the audiences through important locations, archival remnants, and stories related to the Battle of Imphal. The film also casts renowned writer Late Khuraijam Nimaicharan Singh. The film was begun to be made in Imphal Documentor, a 2022 project development lab, functioning for five days, developed by the collaboration between the Manipur State Film Development Society (MSFDS), the Documentary Resource Initiative (DRI), Kolkata, and the Television Cine Foundation Manipur. The film had its world premiere on November 22, 2025, at 9:30 a.m. at INOX – Audi II, Old GMC Building, Campal, Panjim. The film was selected for the Indian Panorama section of the 56th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) 2025, that took place in Goa. The film was shown at the 19th edition of the International Film Festival of India (IFFI), also known as Mumbai International Film Festival (MIFF), on June 20, 2026, which was the oldest and largest celebration of cinema in South Asia. It was considered as one of the two "non-feature" films, that had "drawn attention" in the event, with the another one, being a Marathi language film "Hamsafar", as per the reports of the Press Information Bureau (PIB) of the Government of India. The film Battlefield, along with another Manipuri film Oitharei, simultaneously held the legacy of breaking a year's hiatus (gap) of Manipuri film industry, being absent from annually participating in the International Film Festival of India (IFFI) list. It was announced by the Manipur State Film Development Society (MSFDS) as a "triumphant comeback".

Baywatch is a 2017 American action-comedy movie. It was adapted off the television series of the same name. Principal photography started on February 22, 2016 across Florida and Savannah, Georgia. Baywatch was released in May 2017. The movie got substandard reviews from the critics, mostly for its crude humor and character developments. However, it had a box office intake of just over $58 million in the United States. It made another $119.8 million in several other territories. The total box office intake was around $177.8 million. The movie's budget was $69 million. Baywatch was given five nominations in the 38th Golden Raspberry Awards. The categories were the Worst Prequel, Remake, Rip-off or Sequel, the Worst Screenplay, the Razzie Nominee So Rotten You Loved It and the Worst Picture. Baywatch received an approval rating of only 17% under Rotten Tomatoes. Critics from the movie judging site said: "Baywatch takes its source material's jiggle factor to R-rated levels, but lacks the original's campy charm – and leaves its charming stars flailing in the shallows." It received a rating of 37 out of 100 under Metacritic. That meant "generally unfavorable reviews.". Writing for the Rolling Stone magazine, Peter Travers was happy with the "easy rapport" from Dwayne Johnson and Zac Efron. Travers stated, though, "what [the film] needs more is a functional script". Travers rated the movie two out of four stars. He then said: "Think of yourself sitting down for a big two-hour wallow in instant stupid with a vat of popcorn, slathered in fake butter and possibly a mound of melted M&Ms on top. It feels great chugging it down, then your stomach hurts, your head aches and you puke the whole thing up so you can forget about it in the morning. That's Baywatch in a nutshell." Owen Gleiberman from the Variety magazine called it "stupidly entertaining... for a while". He was, however, not impressed with the movie's plot.

A beach movie or beach party movie is a movie genre. The genre was popular in the late 1950s. It flourished during the early 1960s. The genre was launched in 1959 with Gidget starring Sandra Dee, and came to an end in 1967 with Catalina Caper featuring Tommy Kirk and Little Richard. This movie is generally thought to be the "last gasp" of the genre, the final beach-themed movie. Beach movies are about happy-go-lucky teenagers frolicking on the sun-drenched beaches of California and Hawaii. Genre elements include girlfriend/boyfriend relationships, motorcycles, cars, food, muscles, bikinis, rock and roll, surf music and surfing. Annette Funicello and Frankie Avalon set the pace for the genre as teen sweethearts in a string of seven beach movies from AIP.

The movie was the first of five beach party movies from American International Pictures (AIP). It won the 1964 Golden Laurel "Sleeper of the Year" Award.

Beach Picnic is the animated short film a Donald Duck. Donald Duck is having a picnic at the beach, singing happily. After preparing the food, he tries to ride on an inflatable horse named Seabiscuit, but gets repeatedly bounced off of it, annoying him. Donald then spots Pluto sleeping soundly on the shore, and decides to prank him by pushing Seabiscuit near him and mimicking a horse's whinnying. The mesmerized Pluto tries to chase Seabiscuit around some rocky reefs, but gets repeatedly frightened by the horse bumping him from behind. Getting angry, Pluto bites on the rubber horse's air valve, causing him to inflate like a balloon. As the rubber horse goes completely flat, Pluto is sent flying through the air and crashes onto the shore. The scene cuts to an ant, who spots Donald's food. It calls for the other ants to come and help steal the food. The ants swarm toward the picnic food and start carrying it away. Donald angrily rants at the ants, and then notices some flypaper and decides to use it. An ant secretly tries carrying away a piece of cake. Pluto spots the ant and curiously starts sniffing at it as it runs away. While Pluto follows the ant, Donald has finished setting up his flypaper trap. The ant wisely crawls under the trap, but Pluto gets the flypaper stuck on his nose. After a long struggle, Pluto flies backward and bumps into Donald, causing the flypaper to get stuck on their bottoms. Donald angrily rants at Pluto as they struggle to free themselves, until Pluto, having had enough of Donald's ranting, runs around in circles, tossing Donald into his flypaper trap, causing his body to get wrapped in all of the flypapers like a mummy. As Donald angrily tries to free himself, Pluto runs over to him and starts licking him, ending the cartoon.

A television commercial known for its opening line "There is a bear in the woods" was created for the 1984 U.S. presidential re-election campaign of Ronald Reagan. The commercial shows a grizzly bear wandering through a forest. The narrator of the ad, Hal Riney, talks about how the bear could be dangerous and that it would be smart to be prepared for that possibility. In the final scene a man appears and the bear takes a step back. The ad ends with a picture of Reagan and the tagline: "President Reagan: Prepared for Peace". The bear could have either signified with the massive inflation the United States was facing, Democratic challenger Walter Mondale or the growing tensions of the Soviet Union and the Cold War. Reagan was elected in a massive landslide in the 1984 elections winning 49 of the 50 states.

Beauty and the Beast is a 1991 American animated musical fantasy movie produced by Walt Disney Feature Animation and released by Walt Disney Pictures. It is the 30th movie in the Walt Disney Animated Classics series and the third movie of the Disney Renaissance period. The movie is based on the fairy tale La Belle et la Bête by Jeanne-Marie Le Prince de Beaumont It is about a prince who is turned into a beast and a young woman named Belle whom he imprisons in his castle. It become very popular. This is the first animated feature that was nominated for an Oscar for Best Picture. A direct-to-video sequel called Beauty and the Beast: The Enchanted Christmas was released in 1997. It was followed in 1998 by another sequel, Belle's Magical World. An IMAX special edition version of the original movie was released in 2002, with a new five-minute musical sequence included. Because I Said So is a 2007 romantic comedy movie. The movie is about an overbearing mother who is concerned about her three daughters. Diane Keaton plays Daphne. Mandy Moore plays Milly. Piper Perabo plays Mae. Lauren Graham plays Maggie. Because I Said So got negative reviews from critics. But it did very well at the box office. It took in more than $69 million against a $39 million budget.

Beavis and Butt-Head Do America is an American 1996 comedy and adventure movie. Beavis and Butt-head are the main characters in the movie. They're played by Mike Judge. The teenage boys are from the fictional town of Highland, Texas. David Letterman and Tony Darling as Mötley Crüe roadies Kristofor Brown as Man on plane / Man in confession booth / Old guy / Jim Eric Bogosian as Old Faithful ranger / White House press secretary / Strategic Air Command lieutenant Pamela Blair as Flight attendant / White House tour guide The movie went to theaters in North America on December 20, 1996. It made over $63.1 million at the U.S. box office. It opened at #1 with $20 million. The budget was $12 million. As of September 2015, the movie had a 72% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, based on 54 reviews. On Metacritic, the movie has a 64 out of 100 rating, meaning "generally favorable reviews". Roger Ebert and Gene Siskel gave the movie "two thumbs up". The movie was released on VHS on June 10, 1997. It was released on DVD on November 23, 1999.

Becca's Bunch is a preschool education television series that aired on Nick Jr. from July 2, 2018 to May 10, 2019. Becca (voiced by Noa Fe Williams) is a bird who wears a red knit cap. She is the leader of her bunch and the protagonist of the series. Russell (voiced by Dylan Martin Frankel) is an adventurous squirrel. Pedro (voiced by Ben Stone Zelman) is a fearful ondino bespectacled worm. Sylvia (voiced by Susie Power) is a pink fox. She carries a shoulder bag containing objects which her friends would sometimes use in their adventures. Benny and Shelly (voiced by Lisa Biggs) are Becca's baby brother and sister. They are still in their eggs, though their limbs are sticking out, and are able to walk. Moms (voiced by Amy Stephenson) is Becca's mother. Pops (voiced by Grant George) is Becca's father. Uncle Ned (voiced by William Gaminara) is Pedro's uncle. Ringo (voiced by Guy Harris) is a turtle. Mayor Ladymaus (voiced by Amy Palant) is the mayor of Wagtail Woods. Barry (voiced by Daxx George) is a little bunny. Lola (voiced by Lisa Biggs) is Barry's mother. Casper and Jasper (voiced by Jaden Pace) are the hare brothers, and are somewhat rivals of the bunch. Beatrice (voiced by Sabrina Glow) is a young badger. Gill (voiced by Jason Shablik) is a big fish. Steven (voiced by Paul Tylak) is a seagull, he's the lifeguard of the beach. John Wolfenstein (voiced by Paul Tylak) is a gray wolf, who is a radio personality of Wagtail Woods. Mr. Nugget (voiced by Paul Tylak) is a chicken, who's John Wolfenstein's best friend and colleague. Unlike the other characters, he does not speak but just clucks. MJ (voiced by Joey Camen) is a big moose. Buck (voiced by Joey Camen) is a building beaver

Because of the Cats is a 1973 Dutch Belgian crime drama movie directed by Fons Rademakers and was based on the novel of the same name by Nicolas Freeling. It stars Bryan Marshall, Alexandra Stewart, Sebastian Graham Jones, Edward Judd, Sylvia Kristel, Delia Lindsay, Roger Hammond, George Baker.

Because of Him is a 1946 American romantic comedy movie directed by Richard Wallace and starring Deanna Durbin, Charles Laughton, Franchot Tone, Helen Broderick, Stanley Ridges, Donald Meek, Charles Halton. It was distributed by Universal Pictures.

Beavis and Butt-Head Do the Universe is a 2022 American adult animated comedy movie. It was directed by Jim Reardon and written by Mike Judge and Scott Hemming. The movie was released on December 16, 2022, on Paramount Pictures.

Becker is an American sitcom that was originally first aired on the CBS network on November 2, 1998. It starred Ted Danson as Dr. John Becker, a very grumpy family doctor who is unhappy with his life in The Bronx, New York. Becker became famous for his witty responses and constant negative outlook on all situations. The show was last aired to revived after cancelation on January 28, 2004. For the first four seasons, the main characters were: Becker, a Harvard Medical School graduate, runs a neighborhood medical practice. He is easily annoyed by things, and is a very angry person. He has been married and divorced twice. Becker's office manager, and one of the few people who can not get annoyed by Becker and his ways. Margaret is a motherly-like figure to Becker and Linda. She is married. A muddle-headed girl whose surname is never revealed. She works at the doctor's office to establish independence from her wealthy parents. The owner and worker of a diner she inherited from her late father. Reggie is a former model and is unhappy being stuck running a diner. Becker's best friend. Jake also works at the diner selling newspapers and miscellaneous items such as candy, magazines, cigarettes, gum, etc. Jake is blind following a car accident several years before. Bob loiters at the diner and is Italian. He is an old high school classmate of Reggie's who is short, annoying, and refers to himself in the third person.

Becoming Jane is a movie directed by Julian Jarrold in 2007. The setting of this movie is Hampshire, England in the 1700s. The movie’s story was based on a fictional biography written by Jon Spence. Anne Hathaway played Jane Austen. James McAvoy played Thomas Lefroy. This movie won the 2007 People's Choice Award for "Favorite Independent Movie". It was nominated for 2008 Ivor Novello Award for Best Original Film Score. Jane (played by Anne Hathaway) is a writer. She lives in a rural area. Her father is a pastor of small church. Her family is poor. She is under a lot of stress since her mother wants her to marry Mr. Wisley (Laurence Fox). He is the nephew of the wealthy Lady Gresham (Maggie Smith). Meanwhile, Thomas Lefroy (played by James McAvoy) is working with his uncle as a lawyer in London. He is ordered to go Hampshire due to his dissipated life. When they meet the first time, Tom criticizes Jane’s works and she becomes angry about that. Both of them have hostile feelings toward each other. However, the feelings changes into affection as they meet several times. Finally they decide to marry. With a lot of expectation, they visits Tom’s uncle Judge Langlois. The uncle does not approve of the marriage due to Jane’s poverty. They break up, but since they love each other deeply, they elope. But after knowing about the fact that Tom is the only hope of his family, Jane gives up their elopement and leaves to go home. Twenty years later, Jane becomes famous writer and after a gathering, Jane and Tom meet again. There, Tom is with his daughter who likes Jane’s book a lot. His daughter asks Jane to read the novel. To stop her Tom called his daughter’s name – Jane. Knowing that Tom named his daughter after her, Jane accepts her request and reads her book, Pride and Prejudice.

Becket is a British and American historical drama movie. It is about the historic, tumultuous relationship between King Henry II of England and his friend, the bishop Thomas Becket. It was directed by Peter Glenville and produced by Hal B. Wallis. It stars Peter O'Toole as King Henry II. It also stars John Gielgud and Richard Burton. It was released on March 11, 1964.

Becky is a female nickname for Rebecca (a name found in the Old Testament of the Bible). The term Becky may come from the protagonist Becky Sharp from the 1848 novel Vanity Fair and its connected movie

Bedelia is a 1946 British drama movie directed by Lance Comfort and was based on the 1945 novel of the same name by Vera Caspary. It stars Margaret Lockwood, Ian Hunter, Anne Crawford, Barry K. Barnes, Jill Esmond, Louise Hampton, Olga Lindo and was distributed by General Film Distributors.

"Bedrock Anthem" is a song by "Weird Al" Yankovic. It is a parody of "Under the Bridge" and "Give it Away" by the Red Hot Chili Peppers. It is about the narrator who desires to live in Bedrock, the setting of the cartoon The Flintstones. It states several reasons referring to the show. It was released on the 1993 album Alapalooza.

Bedknobs and Broomsticks is a 1971 musical movie produced by Walt Disney Productions. It combines live action and animation. It was released in North America on December 13, 1971. It is based on the books The Magic Bed Knob; or, How to Become a Witch in Ten Easy Lessons and Bonfires and Broomsticks by English children's author Mary Norton. The movie is often compared to Mary Poppins. It is also partly set in the streets of London. It shares some of the cast from Mary Poppins, a similar crew, the same songwriters and director. The movie was made at Walt Disney Studios. The castle scenes were shot on location at Corfe Castle, Dorset, England, UK. Angela Lansbury as Miss Eglantine Price, an apprentice witch. David Tomlinson as Emelius Browne, Miss Price's former teacher and headmaster of Correspondence College of Witchcraft.
